data.one_liner: A wrapper for shared_preferences to cache data with lifetime support.
data.what_it_does: Wraps shared_preferences to simplify storing and loading strings, maps, and lists. It supports setting expiration lifetimes for cached items and retrieving default values if a key does not exist.
use_when: You want a simpler API over shared_preferences for basic caching needs.
You need to cache API responses or app data with a time-to-live (TTL) expiration.
You work with common data types like String, Map, List<String>, and List<Map>.
avoid_when: You need complex relational queries or large-scale local storage (use a database like sqflite or drift instead).
You need secure encryption for stored data (use flutter_secure_storage instead).
strengths: Simplifies working with shared_preferences via functional helpers like cache.remember.
Supports optional cache lifetimes in seconds.
Automatically handles multiple data types including nested maps and lists.
weaknesses: Limited to data types supported by or serializable through shared_preferences.
Relies entirely on shared_preferences underneath, inheriting its performance and storage limits.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: It is the underlying official key-value store plugin if you prefer direct control without wrappers.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your cached data requires encryption and secure storage.
